comment: Frontier projection over docs/semantic/zones/*.json and the four relations_<lens>.json files. open_antecedents clusters the antecedent mentions carried by the statement nodes into distinct unproved hypotheses. expert_questions selects exact human handoffs with checked consumers and explicit closure scope. engine_hierarchy orders the engines by the strength of the hypothesis they demand and records, per barrier, exactly which sibling engines the barrier does NOT reach. bare_equivalences lists the proved iffs whose two sides are both open, i.e. the restatements. nonrecurring_candidates is deliberately short and is not a novelty claim: prior_art_state is not_assessed for almost all of it and every entry states its own residual risk.
method: Logical class was taken from the zone files, which read it off the Lean statement rather than the docstring. A node counts as blocked only where a barrier_for edge or a scope caveat names it. 'closest_producer' is the node that comes nearest to realising the hypothesis, never a node that discharges it; null means nothing in either library bears on it. The barrier/engine reading follows relations_barrier_engine.json, whose non_edges are the load-bearing half: a barrier with unrecorded unreached siblings is the failure mode that produced the earlier squarefree overclaim.

expert_questions.exact_ask: Prove that for every starting scale t0 there is t >= t0 and a finite depth L for which certifiedKill (periodLcm t) (periodLcm t) L holds.
expert_questions.payoff: This is equivalent to irrationality of the totient constant, so a proof closes Erdős #249.
expert_questions.boundary: This is an exact normal form of #249, not a weaker intermediate problem and not progress until the unbounded quantifier is proved.
expert_questions.known_obstruction: The checked diagonal band stops at t = 82 and the off-diagonal roster is finite; neither supplies certificates beyond every bound.
expert_questions.current_hypothesis: The cofinal diagonal supply holds, equivalently the totient constant is irrational. Confidence is low because the checked band is bounded and the equivalence gives no asymptotic mechanism.

plausible_alternatives.consequence: By the checked equivalence, Erdős #249 is true.

plausible_alternatives.statement: Some starting scale has no later diagonal certificate.
plausible_alternatives.consequence: By the same equivalence, the totient constant is rational.

current_evidence: A diagonal certificate is checked at every t <= 82.
Historical off-diagonal audit: 125 verified rows represent 123 distinct (h,N,L) certificates in 122 Lean files. This finite roster is asymptotically nondiscriminating.

Exact arithmetic gives 960/960 certificates on 1 <= N <= 120, 1 <= h <= 8, with first-depth excess 0 through 11 over the admissibility floor (median 1, mean 727/480). Across the 33 distinct LCM scales filling positive t <= 82, checked working-depth excess is 0 through 4 (median 1, mean 40/33), but only five depths are proved least. Finite low excess proves no asymptotic law, bounded-excess theorem, or cofinal supply.

A rational representation of the totient constant, or a proof that the diagonal predicate fails beyond some scale, establishes eventual_diagonal_failure.
More bounded certificates without an asymptotic argument do not distinguish the alternatives.

expert_questions.boundary: The exact four-term decomposition and consumer are proved; no prime-distribution or residual-decorrelation theorem supplying the budgets is proved.
expert_questions.known_obstruction: A bound on the total complex norm is stronger than needed; the live socket needs only the one-sided centred real bound, but still needs a cofinal arithmetic producer.

We expect the centred real term, rather than total complex norm, to be the hard budget. Confidence is low because none of the four budgets has a cofinal producer.

plausible_alternatives.consequence: This pivot socket fails; #249 may still be true by another mechanism.

expert_questions.payoff: Together with the six checked initial levels, this proves that 1/2 belongs to the Mersenne achievement set. The checked finite-support exclusion then forces the witnessing support to be infinite, giving a rational counterexample to universal Erdős #257.

A naive common-denominator construction gives only an upper height bound on the scale 2^O(n^2), with no matching reduced-denominator lower bound.

Thus the prime-gap socket is a question about one initial unit-modulus squaring orbit plus prime sampling, not a new finite-window estimate; entering a dyadic root is an explicit barrier, not an established event.
